positions.name: AsyncJobContractAsSettledRule
positions.frame: How does the async job contract get settled as an operational rule — stated as mechanism rather than argued for?
positions.why: Both expressions perform the async job contract as a settled decision rather than a position under debate. src-1 ratifies it with operational guarantees (immediate receipt, polling cursor, no blocking, no lost work on client drop); src-2 declares the key decision's dispatch-and-delivery mechanism (poll or piggyback). The shared directional read is that the contract's authority comes from stating how the mechanism works as settled fact. Tension exists in the relational footing — communal 'We ratified' (src-1) versus authoritative 'Key decision' (src-2) — but both perform the same move: declaring the contract's behavior as operational rule the speaker expects others to follow.
